reconcile.note: Clarke resolves the placement dispute by proposing Jesus cleansed the temple twice, opening his ministry as John records and closing it as the Synoptics record.

discrepancy.note: Strauss weighs whether John and the Synoptics record one temple-cleansing or two and concludes the chronological gap cannot be resolved by simple harmony.

quotes.text: Jesus, during his first residence in Jerusalem, according to John ( ii. 14 ff. ), according to the synoptists, during his last ( Matt. xxi. 12 ff. parall.), undertook the purification of the temple.
quotes.attr: David Friedrich Strauss (d. 1874), The Life of Jesus Critically Examined, trans. George Eliot (1846), §88, on John 2:14 and Matthew 21:12.

sides.snippet: Jesus entered into the temple, and began to throw out those who sold and those who bought in the temple, and overthrew the tables of the money-changers, and the seats of those who sold the doves.
sides.verseText: They came to Jerusalem, and Jesus entered into the temple, and began to throw out those who sold and those who bought in the temple, and overthrew the tables of the money-changers, and the seats of those who sold the doves.

sides.snippet: He made a whip of cords, and threw all out of the temple, both the sheep and the oxen; and he poured out the changers' money, and overthrew their tables.
sides.verseText: He made a whip of cords, and threw all out of the temple, both the sheep and the oxen; and he poured out the changers' money, and overthrew their tables.
